governanceNotes: This draft edge is authored under degenerative-disc-disease as the service-connected primary. It is intended to support a bounded anatomical association framing (degenerative disc disease can be associated with anatomically concordant radiculopathy) rather than a direct individual causation claim; the nexus classification is ASSOCIATION_ONLY.

Where the veteran's radiculopathy is not anatomically concordant with the service-connected DDD level, or where another cause (e.g., peripheral entrapment, plexus lesion, spinal stenosis unrelated to the DDD level, myelopathy, systemic neuropathy) explains the findings, this edge must not be used.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Degenerative disc disease and radiculopathy are reported to be associated when a degenerated disc at a given level is anatomically concordant with symptoms and findings in the corresponding nerve root distribution; the located evidence supports an anatomical/pathophysiological association rather than a proven individual causation chain, so the relationship is carried here as a bounded clinical proposition pending individual-degree medical nexus evidence.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by the current evidence at the level of an automatic individual causal chain; the association is anatomical and level-specific and requires individualized corroboration.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Degenerative disc disease is hypothesized to be associated with radiculopathy through disc height loss, annular disruption, and disc bulging/herniation that may contact or compress the anatomically corresponding nerve root, with possible chemical radiculitis from disc material, so that the level-specific degenerative change can be associated with radicular symptoms in the corresponding dermatomal/myotomal distribution.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Age-related degenerative change, segmental instability, and Modic changes may accompany the compressive component and influence symptom generation without by themselves establishing individual causation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The located evidence supports an anatomical association between degenerative disc disease and radiculopathy when there is level-specific concordance, but it does not, by itself, establish that a service-connected degenerative disc disease caused or aggravated an individual veteran's radiculopathy; the edge is constrained to association pending objective corroboration of level-specific nerve-root involvement and exclusion of competing causes.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Level-specific anatomical concordance between the service-connected DDD and the claimed radiculopathy; imaging evidence (MRI/CT) and examination findings consistent with the corresponding nerve-root distribution; exclusion of competing causes (peripheral entrapment, plexus lesion, foraminal stenosis from other etiology, central stenosis/myelopathy, systemic neuropathy, non-degenerate structural lesion); individual medical nexus opinion linking the service-connected DDD to the radiculopathy.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Peripheral entrapment neuropathy at a site outside the spine
Plexopathy or proximal nerve lesion unrelated to the DDD level
Foraminal or central stenosis from non-degenerate etiology
Spinal cord disease or myelopathy rather than isolated radiculopathy
Nondegenerative structural lesion (e.g., tumor, infection, fracture) causing radiculopathy

suggestions.rationale: Degenerative disc disease can be associated with radiculopathy when there is anatomical concordance at the corresponding level, but the evidence supports an anatomical/biomechanical association rather than an automatic individual causal chain; the edge is constrained to association because it requires level-specific imaging and examination corroboration and exclusion of competing causes before any individual nexus can be asserted.

pathwayIntelligence.causalChain: service-connected degenerative disc disease -> (hypothesized) disc height loss / annular disruption / bulge-herniation with possible nerve-root contact or chemical radiculitis at the anatomically concordant level -> radiculopathy in the corresponding distribution; association only pending individual nexus and level-specific corroboration
developmentQuestions: What is the level of the service-connected degenerative disc disease, and is the claimed radiculopathy in the anatomically concordant nerve-root distribution?
Is there imaging evidence of nerve-root contact, compression, or herniation at that level, and do examination findings match the dermatomal/myotomal distribution?
Have competing causes of the radicular symptoms been excluded or accounted for?
issuesToResolve: Determine whether the radiculopathy is level-concordant with the service-connected DDD or whether a different etiology better explains the findings.
Assess whether chemical radiculitis vs. mechanical compression is the more plausible mediator for this veteran's presentation.

evidenceGaps: Level-specific anatomical concordance between service-connected DDD and claimed radiculopathy
Imaging and examination corroboration of the corresponding nerve-root distribution
Exclusion of peripheral entrapment, plexopathy, non-degenerate stenosis, myelopathy, systemic neuropathy, and other structural lesions
Individual medical nexus opinion linking the service-connected DDD to the radiculopathy
